name: Question 5
worked_solution:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the $x$-axis:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-16 & =0 \\ {x}^{4} & =16 \\ \sqrt[4]{{x}^{4}} & =\sqrt[4]{16} \\ x & =\pm \sqrt[4]{{2}^{4}} \\ x & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

The only solution between $x=0$ and $x=3$ is $x=2.$

Since $2\in [0,3],$ we have two regions: 

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=2.$

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=2$ to $x=3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14038781/assets/bf221ae10e68a9c17efadd82b39264807b4dc00774fae7e30d9c0c9907368698.png)

Notice that the region for $x\in [0,2]$ lies completely below the $x$-axis. Hence, the value of

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{4}-16)\text{d}x
$$

will be negative.

Therefore, the area that we want is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{4}-16)\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x+16{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}\,{|}_{0}^{2}+16x\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}[{2}^{5}-{0}^{5}]+16[2-0] \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}(32-0)+16(2) \\  & =-\frac{32}{5}+32 \\  & =-\frac{32}{5}+\frac{160}{5} \\  & =\frac{128}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x\in [2,3],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{2}^{3}({x}^{4}-16)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x-16{\int }_{2}^{3}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}\,{|}_{2}^{3}-16x\,{|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[{3}^{5}-{2}^{5}]-16[3-2] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(243-32)-16(1) \\  & =\frac{211}{5}-16 \\  & =\frac{211}{5}-\frac{80}{5} \\  & =\frac{131}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the total area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =\frac{128}{5}+\frac{131}{5} \\  & =\frac{259}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
